summary: The candidate successfully extracts every central paper result: the general gluing isomorphism, all three handle-attachment formulas, both principal supporting lemmas, and most of the defining algebraic infrastructure. Its formulas are generally faithful and LaTeX is well formed. It falls short of flawless quality because several external foundations are absent or mistyped, some hypotheses are compressed, the gluing theorem and Lemma 3.9 are duplicated across overlapping chunks, and several proof constructions are promoted to independent definitions. Page attribution also differs from the Gold reference for the introductory handle results.
strengths: All four core results in the Gold artifact are represented: the gluing theorem and the 1-, 2-, and 3-handle formulas.
The parameterized-triple module, associated 3-manifold algebra, and balanced gluing map are extracted with substantially correct mathematical content.
Both Gold supporting lemmas are covered, including the algebra/module evaluation isomorphisms and the identification with Khovanov's tangle invariant.
The Ren-Willis gluing surjection is explicitly marked as external and supplied with a source reference.
The candidate preserves the key tensor-product base algebra in at least one version of Theorem 4.1 and correctly describes the construction of the gluing map and its inverse.
Displayed formulas have balanced delimiters and no major LaTeX corruption.
issues: The axiomatic definition of a functorial link homology theory is missing as an independent entry.
The foundational Morrison-Walker-Wedrich Skein Lasagna theory and Khovanov tangle-bimodule functor are not separately extracted as externally attributed results.
The evaluation isomorphism is split into a calculation and an external proposition rather than represented cleanly as the externally sourced theorem in the Gold artifact.
The Ren-Willis external result is typed as a proposition rather than matching the Gold theorem classification.
The triple-module definition compresses framing, embedding, and boundary-intersection hypotheses into a generic phrase, weakening statement precision.
The introductory gluing entry omits the explicit subscript algebra on the tensor product; later duplicate versions restore it.
The gluing theorem appears three times and Lemma 3.9 twice because overlap entries were not deduplicated.
Several proof-level constructions, including the inverse map and intermediate surface J, are classified as definitions, producing unnecessary fragmentation.
The entry paper:thm:general-handle-attachment is marked external while citing this paper's own Theorem 4.1 and is not a distinct Gold theorem.
The three overview handle theorems use page 2, whereas the corresponding Gold source locators point to page 1.

entryLevelComparison.note: No standalone extraction of the functorial link homology axioms.
The direct-sum definition is correct, but several geometric and framing hypotheses are only summarized.
The direct sum and gluing multiplication are represented correctly; local units are omitted.
Domain, base algebra, compatible-boundary union, and zero case are all captured.
MWW appears only as the source of the evaluation map, not as the general foundational theory used by the paper.
Mathematical content and external attribution are present, but the result is fragmented and mistyped.
Its consequences occur in the module-identification lemma, but the external functorial construction is not independently extracted.
The statement and attribution are substantially correct, with a theorem-versus-proposition classification discrepancy.
Both the algebra and module isomorphisms are faithfully represented.
The result is accurate but duplicated; both copies also preserve the apparent source indexing b in H^n rather than normalizing it.
Theorem 4.1 is covered accurately, but repeated three times; only the most complete copy explicitly names the balancing algebra.
The Hochschild-homology conclusion and cocore-cut tangle hypothesis are correctly retained.
The cabling quotient by the solid-torus algebra action is captured, though less precisely than the Gold formulation using the specified subalgebra.
The quotient-module description induced by the associated algebra action is retained.
